description: issue #687 (slice I8), extended by #681 (slice I2): with the `interaction-events` profile active, a program that actually USES all six implemented Interaction forms — the `wait` and `input` primitives and the `when`/`every`/`on_key`/`on_click` block-heads — checks clean. The block-heads were already visible names (slices I3-I6); `wait` was NOT, so before I8 this program raised `ol-unknown-command` on line 2 even under an active profile — a profile whose own primitive is unknown is not conformant. I8 registers the profile's primitives in `collectVisibleNames`' `interaction-events` gate, and this fixture is the proof the gap is closed (since issue #966 that gate is a sweep of the profile-keyed registry, so the wiring is automatic rather than a per-profile accessor call). `input` joined that same table in its own slice (#681), which ships its evaluator: I8 deliberately left it out because registering a known callee with no runtime behind it would let a program check clean and then fail at runtime, and #681 closes both halves together. `wait` and `input` are placed inside a procedure body (with `wait` further inside a `[ ... ]` block inside `repeat`) so a fix that only handled a top-level occurrence cannot pass. This is a check-mode fixture: it proves static NAME VISIBILITY and arity only — it does not execute, so it asserts nothing about handler delivery or about the read itself (the sibling directories' execution fixtures cover those).
